title: Part-Part-Whole: Splitting and Joining to 10
seo_title: Foundation Part-Part-Whole Worksheets: Number Bonds and Ways to Make 10 (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Partition and combine collections up to 10 using part-part-whole relationships and subitising to recognise and name the parts.
meta_desc: Free Foundation (Prep, Kindergarten) maths worksheets on part-part-whole to 10, matched to the Australian Curriculum (AC9MFN04): parts make the whole, hidden parts, number bonds and ways to make 5 and 10. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: Two parts make the whole. The parts are smaller than the whole.
key_sub: Number bonds show the whole and its parts. 6 and 4, 7 and 3, 5 and 5 all make 10.
body_html:
Two parts make a whole

A group can be split into two parts. Put the parts together to get the whole.

Number bonds

A number bond shows the whole on top and the two parts below. If one part is missing, think: what goes with this part to make the whole?

Ways to make 10

A ten-frame shows two parts of 10: 6 red and 4 blue. Other ways: 9 and 1, 8 and 2, 7 and 3, 5 and 5.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Giving the whole when a part is missingFind what goes with the part you know
Giving the part you can seeSome are hidden: count on to the whole
Adding the whole and the partThe parts are always smaller than the whole

faq.a: It is the idea that a whole group can be split into two parts, and the parts join back to make the whole. Foundation students partition and combine collections up to 10 (AC9MFN04).
A diagram with the whole at the top and two parts underneath, such as 7 split into 4 and 3. It shows how numbers are made of other numbers.

faq.q: Why practise the ways to make 10?
faq.a: Knowing pairs like 6 and 4 or 7 and 3 helps children add and subtract quickly in Year 1 and Year 2.

faq.q: How can I practise at home?
faq.a: Hide some of 10 pegs under a cup and ask how many are hidden. Split a handful of grapes into two plates and say the parts and the whole.
